ov: Arachnids with eight legs, grasping pincers and a curved tail ending in a venomous sting. More than 2,500 species live on every continent except Antarctica, mostly in deserts. All give birth to live young.

why.dg: Most stings don’t need medical treatment, but about 25 species, under 1%, can kill a person. Deaths happen mainly where medical help is hard to reach.
why.p: Often kept as pets, needing little more than a secure, lockable tank.
why.ac: Its eyes are sensitive enough for night species to navigate by starlight.
why.et: Eaten in West Africa, Myanmar and East Asia; fried scorpion is a tradition in Shandong, China.

df: Mostly insects and other invertebrates; some take vertebrates. It digests food outside its body.
fx: A mother carries her young on her back until their exoskeletons harden.
